IdentityA marksman who plants their feet and makes every shot count, with exploding dice, steady nerves and grit that won't go down.

Level by Level at a Glance

What you gain and when. Full details are under Class Abilities.

LvlYou gain
1Firearm Proficiency, Quick Draw, Dead Eye, Grit, kit, feat
2Lightning Reload
3Dead Aim, feat
4Called Shot
5Two-Gun Shot (Extra Attack)
6Perfect Shot, feat
7Steady Shot
8Trick Shot
9Brace and Fire, Perfect Shot improves, kit improves
10Fan the Hammer, Called Shot without Disadvantage, Renown: Name

Class Abilities

1st Level

Firearm Proficiency

  • Effect: Use blackpowder weapons without Disadvantage.
  • Firearm damage is exploding: when a damage die shows its highest number, roll it again and add the result (see Exploding Dice in The Arneyan Codex).
  • Non-Gunslingers follow the Firearms training rules in The Arneyan Codex

Quick Draw

  • Effect: Drawing a loaded sidearm (pistol) doesn't use your one free object use this turn.
  • The weapon must already be loaded
  • Drawing an unloaded weapon and loading it still costs a full action

Dead Eye

  • Effect: On a turn you don't move, your first ranged attack's damage dice explode on either of their two highest numbers (see Exploding Dice in The Arneyan Codex).
  • You cannot move before or after attacking: once you attack with Dead Eye you are rooted until the end of your turn, and if you have already moved this turn you gain no benefit. Forced movement (being shoved, knocked prone and so on) does not count

Grit

  • Effect: Once per day, when you are reduced to 0 HP or below, you stay at 1 HP instead.

2nd Level

Lightning Reload

  • Effect: All blackpowder weapons reload one round faster (minimum: reload as part of an attack, once per round).
  • Combined with Quick Draw, a Gunslinger can draw, fire, and reload in a single round, ready to fire again next round

3rd Level

Dead Aim

  • Effect: If you did not move or attack last turn, your first shot this turn has Advantage and deals +1d6 damage.
    • 15th level: its bonus damage rises to +2d6.

4th Level

Called Shot

  • Effect: You can make Called Shots (see Combat Manoeuvres in The Arneyan Codex); from 10th level they don't take the Disadvantage.

5th Level

Two-Gun Shot

  • Effect: When you use your action to attack, make one additional weapon attack as part of it, with Disadvantage (see Extra attacks in The Arneyan Codex).
  • A firearm still has to be loaded for each shot.
  • No Disadvantage when the extra shot is fired from a second loaded firearm, drawn as part of the attack, so no reload.

6th Level

Perfect Shot

  • Effect: Once per day, declare before rolling. If the shot hits, two of its damage dice explode once, whatever they rolled: roll each again and add it (the new die explodes as normal).
  • More dice: three dice at 9th level.
    • 15th level: every damage die, and twice per day.

7th Level

Steady Shot

  • Effect: While Dead Eye applies, the first attack that hits each round deals +1d6 bonus damage.
  • Stacks with Dead Aim; both bonuses are added on the same shot

8th Level

Trick Shot (Dexterity)

  • Effect: Perform an impossible-looking shot: DC determined by the GM based on difficulty, using the General Difficulty Tiers table.
  • Shoot around corners, ricochet off surfaces, disarm a target at range within 30ft
  • Pin clothing or hair to a surface, cut a rope, thread a needle
  • One attempt per round: a failed check simply misses

9th Level

Brace and Fire

  • Effect: When a creature charges you, once per round, out of turn, make one ranged attack against it before it reaches you; Dead Eye applies to it whether or not you moved.
  • If the attack hits, the charging creature takes damage and must make a Fortitude save or stop the charge

10th Level

Fan the Hammer

  • Effect: Once per encounter, as your action, fire every loaded firearm you carry, one shot each, at one or more targets in range. None of these shots takes Two-Gun Shot's Disadvantage.

Renown: Name

  • Effect: Your deeds are known. Title: Shootist. In any town a bounty is open for you, and lawmen let you collect it without question. Your first follower, a powder-boy, joins you.

13th Level

Powder Master

  • Effect: You can set blackpowder charges to breach a door or wall, bring down a rockface or blast a tunnel. The GM says how much powder and time a job needs.

15th Level

  • Dexterity Bonus: permanent +1 Dexterity. It can take the score past 20, to 22 at most (see The Mortal Limit in Character Creation).
  • Renown: Holding: you may found an armoury as your Holding (see Your Holding (15th) in Keeps & Kingdoms).
  • Perfect Shot and Dead Aim improve, as their entries say.

17th Level

Gunsmith

  • Effect: In downtime you can build or modify firearms, and make powder and shot, at half the cost.

20th Level

Legendary Shot

  • Effect: Once per encounter, make a single ranged attack against any target in line of sight regardless of range: no distance penalties apply, and every damage die of it explodes once, whatever it rolled.

Renown: Company

  • Effect: Your stronghold becomes your gun company (see Renown in The Arneyan Codex); each season 2d6 shooters and an armourer join it. While you hold it, firearms supplied from it misfire on one number fewer (a Misfire of 1-2 becomes 1); a natural 1 still misfires.

Kits: Gunslinger Traditions

Each kit is an item in the Kits compendium, in the Gunslinger folder. Drag one onto your character.

Choose one Kit at character creation.

  • Your kit defines the tradition, culture, and context that shaped your relationship with blackpowder.
  • Each kit reshapes one of your 1st-level features, as its Reshapes line says, and improves at 9th level.
  • The peoples, orders and places a kit names are examples, not the only ones: a kit suits anyone from a tradition like it.
